subject: cuttlefish
title: Scientists Gave Cuttlefish the Marshmallow Test. They Passed

scenes.text: A cuttlefish turned down food on purpose. For two minutes.
Cambridge scientists gave six cuttlefish the marshmallow test of self-control.
A raw king prawn was there at once. Behind a second door: live grass shrimp, their favourite, after a wait.
Every one waited, up to 130 seconds, as long as chimps, crows and parrots manage.
When the shrimp door could never open, they stopped waiting and ate the prawn.
The most patient ones also learned fastest. Two minutes of waiting, for a shrimp.

description:
Common cuttlefish passed a version of the famous marshmallow test, the test of delayed gratification.
In a 2021 study in Proceedings of the Royal Society B, Alexandra Schnell of the University of Cambridge and colleagues offered six cuttlefish a raw king prawn immediately or their preferred live grass shrimp after a delay. All six waited, tolerating delays of 50 to 130 seconds, comparable to chimpanzees, crows and parrots. When the shrimp could never be reached, they ate the prawn at once. The cuttlefish with the most self-control were also the fastest learners in a reversal task.
How long would you wait for your favourite meal?
first_comment: A cuttlefish lives about two years, so two minutes is a real sacrifice. Which animal would you bet on in the marshmallow test?
